title: Audit event capture patterns for interactive admin operations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Define practical, implementation-ready event capture patterns for interactive administrative operations (UI/API/CLI) that balance forensic fidelity, privacy, and storage cost. This ticket consolidates what to log, how to encode actor and target identity for RBAC v2, and an opinionated diff format for state changes. Focus: interactive admin flows (grant/revoke roles, policy edits, organization/project transfers, sensitive CRUD on secrets/policies).
outcome_expectation: Produce a single-page reference spec + example encoder library sketch and a compatibility guide for existing audit pipeline consumers (log ingest, SIEM, incident playbooks).
sample_event_schema:
event_id: string
timestamp: RFC3339 string
severity: info|warning|critical
event_type: admin.change|admin.access|admin.failed_auth|admin.login
actor: { id, type, identity_source } encoded as string refs (see actor_resolution)
actor_resolution: stable canonicalization string (user:<id>@provider) plus enriched fields in ingest layer, example: 'u:12345:okta'
target: string (resource path)
target_type: role|policy|service_account|secret|org|project
change_summary: short human text
diff_encoding: json-patch|op-list|compact-delta
pre_ref: storage pointer or hashed snapshot id (avoid storing PII in event)
post_ref: storage pointer or hashed snapshot id
diff_ops: optional inline small diffs (base64 compressed) for low-volume ops
redaction_mask: list of fields redacted with justification tag
auth_context: method:saml|oidc|token|session, session_id, saml_assertion_ref
request_meta: request_id, route, client_ip, geo, user_agent
risk_score: low|medium|high (ingest-calculated)
retention_class: audit|short|sensitive
links: list of external artifact refs (PR, runbook, dashboard)
notes: free text for operator-supplied context
encoding_decision: We recommend hybrid approach: primary persistent envelope is small and normalized (fixed keys above), with diffs encoded either as JSON Patch when diffs are primarily structural and small, or as a compact op-list for long form changes (field, op, short-hash). Large pre/post images should be referenced by snapshot id rather than inlined. Inline diffs allowed only when compressed size < 4KB.
actor_target_resolution_rules: Actors should be recorded as stable, provider-qualified IDs (e.g., okta|gcp|internal) plus a canonical resolution token used across systems. Targets should be recorded as hierarchical resource paths (e.g., /orgs/123/projects/456/policies/deny-ssh). For service-to-service changes include service identity and key id. Sensitive actor attributes (email) may be optionally redacted in the envelope and stored in a separate resolved identity store with controlled access.
diff_format_examples:
Example A - small policy toggle (json-patch): [ {"op":"replace", "path":"/rules/0/allow", "value":false } ]
Example B - role membership op-list: [ {op: 'remove_member', path: '/roles/admin', member_ref: 'u:12345:okta'}, {op: 'add_member', path: '/roles/ops', member_ref: 'u:67890:internal'} ]
Example C - compact delta encoding for audit lane: field|op|short-hash e.g. 'rules.0.allow|R|a1b2c3'
redaction_and_privacy: All events must include a redaction_mask explaining what was removed and why. Personally Identifiable Information (emails, IPs depending on region) should be removed according to retention_class and regulatory label. We favor 'pointer + resolved store' pattern: compact envelope in logs, full resolved identity stored in an encrypted identity service with RBAC-gated lookup. This minimizes exposure in logs and SIEM exports.
storage_and_cost_guidance: Retention_class determines TTL: 'audit' = 7 years (enterprise), 'short' = 90 days. Inline diffs and pre/post images are stored only when retention tier and cost budget allow; otherwise store snapshots in cold object store with hashed pointers in envelope. Compress inline diffs with zstd. Alert: capture volume estimation required—admins often cause many small changes; set throttling in UI to coalesce identical quick edits into single change frames where semantically safe.
instrumentation_notes: UI/CLI/HTTP server libraries should emit the normalized envelope and tag events with request_id. Client libraries should provide helpers: begin_change_frame(), record_pre_snapshot(), apply_change(), finalize_frame(). On error paths emit admin.failed_auth with available context and classification. All saml/oidc assertions should be referenced by assertion_id rather than whole assertion payload.
testing_and_validation: Add unit tests for encoder/decoder roundtrip, property tests for redaction_mask application, and e2e tests that verify downstream consumers (ingest pipeline, SIEM connector, retention job) accept both json-patch and compact op-list encodings. Create corpus of synthetic admin sessions for load testing.
migration_strategy: Phase 1: emit new envelope in parallel (dual-write) alongside existing audit events for 6 weeks. Phase 2: require new envelope for all interactive admin routes, keep legacy for backwards compatibility for another 3 months. Provide a translation shim for older consumers (lambda) to map new envelope to legacy schema.
rollout_plan: 1) Draft spec and internal review (security, infra) - 2 weeks. 2) Implement encoder libs in backend and UI - 3 weeks. 3) Dual-write rollout to staging - 1 week. 4) Monitor volume and correctness, fix edge cases - 2 weeks. 5) Gradual prod enablement by org - 2 weeks.
tradeoffs: We trade off maximal fidelity (storing full pre/post images inline) for cost and privacy by preferring hashed snapshot references. Inline diffs improve immediate forensic ability but increase index/search costs. Using JSON Patch maximizes compatibility, compact op-list reduces size for repeated admin ops but requires consumers to understand higher-level operations.
open_questions: 1) Should we standardize a single diff encoding or support both indefinitely? 2) How do we handle rollbacks: do we log revert operations as separate frames or as annotated diffs? 3) Access controls for resolved identity store: default RBAC rules?
next_steps: 1) Host design review with Security and Infra (scheduled 2026-02-26). 2) Prototype encoder as a Go/TypeScript package and a minimalist shim for existing pipeline. 3) Produce PRD page and import into runbook library.
